reason: This text is the Song of Moses (Exodus 15), a triumphant hymn celebrating Israel's deliverance from Egypt and God's power. It contains no discussion of the Hebrew people suffering greatly, nor any leaders attributing blame to the people for suffering. The passage focuses entirely on celebrating God's military victory over Pharaoh's forces, God's majesty, and God's guidance and protection of the people. There is no element of suffering attribution or blame.
